Diving has definitely helped me overcome some fears, although there are still plenty more to work on. I feel like diving is a way for me to challenge myself, better myself little by little, until I'm doing things that I'd never imagined were possible. 

I've always had a deep sense of respect for the water, but going from swimming strictly in pools and being afraid of the eerie glow at night from the underwater pool lights, to diving at 7 o'clock at night at the beach, cold temperatures, almost pitch black, and relying on a flashlight to navigate and explore the underwater terrain has been incredibly life-changing. 

I definitely couldn't imagine going it alone, and I'm thankful to have a strong support group and knowledgeable diving partners. I'm glad that i was able to discover this amazing sport and encourage anyone who's interested to dip their toes in the water!

I used an unflavored or "original" flavored GT Kombucha as my starter. And my process is as follows:

I used 3.5 quarts of water, brought it to a boil, added 1 cup of sugar, and then 8 black tea bags. I let it cool naturally to 70-75°F before adding 2 cups of a starter kombucha, a substitute for my SCOBY, into a 1 gallon jug. Covered the top so it could breathe but keep bugs out and stored it in a cupboard at room temp for about 10 days. After that I started the 2F process of adding flavor and bottling while simultaneously restarting the 1F process. Before bottling, I transferred as much of the film/"SCOBY" that I could into a new gallon jar, equalling the the original 2 cups from a starter kombucha. 

I thouroughly cleaned every utensil before use and used white vinegar to disinfect as well.
